en: Job 39

p.src: 1  “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?

en: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
u.src: 1  “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?

p.src: 2  Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?

en: Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?
u.src: 2  Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?

p.src: 3  They bow themselves. They bear their young. They end their labor pains.

en: They bow themselves. They bear their young. They end their labor pains.
u.src: 3  They bow themselves. They bear their young. They end their labor pains.

p.src: 4  Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.

en: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.
u.src: 4  Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.

p.src: 5  “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,

en: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
u.src: 5  “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,

p.src: 6  whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?

en: whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
u.src: 6  whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?

p.src: 7  He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.

en: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
u.src: 7  He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.

p.src: 8  The range of the mountains is his pasture. He searches after every green thing.

en: The range of the mountains is his pasture. He searches after every green thing.
u.src: 8  The range of the mountains is his pasture. He searches after every green thing.

p.src: 9  “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?

en: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
u.src: 9  “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?

p.src: 10  Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?

en: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
u.src: 10  Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?

p.src: 11  Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?

en: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?
u.src: 11  Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?

p.src: 12  Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?

en: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?
u.src: 12  Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?

p.src: 13  “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they the feathers and plumage of love?

en: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they the feathers and plumage of love?
u.src: 13  “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they the feathers and plumage of love?

p.src: 14  For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,

en: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,
u.src: 14  For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,

p.src: 15  and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.

en: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.
u.src: 15  and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.

p.src: 16  She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,

en: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
u.src: 16  She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,

p.src: 17  because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.

en: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
u.src: 17  because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.

p.src: 18  When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.

en: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
u.src: 18  When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.

p.src: 19  “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?

en: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
u.src: 19  “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?

p.src: 20  Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.

en: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
u.src: 20  Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.

p.src: 21  He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.

en: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
u.src: 21  He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.

p.src: 22  He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.

en: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
u.src: 22  He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.

p.src: 23  The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.

en: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
u.src: 23  The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.

p.src: 24  He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.

en: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
u.src: 24  He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.

p.src: 25  As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

en: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
u.src: 25  As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

p.src: 26  “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?

en: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
u.src: 26  “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?

p.src: 27  Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?

en: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
u.src: 27  Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?

p.src: 28  On the cliff he dwells and makes his home, on the point of the cliff and the stronghold.

en: On the cliff he dwells and makes his home, on the point of the cliff and the stronghold.
u.src: 28  On the cliff he dwells and makes his home, on the point of the cliff and the stronghold.

p.src: 29  From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.

en: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
u.src: 29  From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.

p.src: 30  His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”

en: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
u.src: 30  His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
